keyVerseText: And he said unto them, This is that which the LORD hath said, To morrow is the rest of the holy sabbath unto the LORD: bake that which ye will bake to day, and seethe that ye will seethe; and that which remaineth over lay up for you to be kept until the morning.
rootMeaning: The Hebrew word שַׁבָּתוֹן (shabbâthôwn) derives from the root שַׁבָּת (shabbâth), which fundamentally means 'to cease' or 'to rest.' This root conveys the idea of cessation from labor or activity, emphasizing a divinely instituted pause. The addition of the suffix in שַׁבָּתוֹן intensifies this concept, referring specifically to a sabbatism or special holy rest. Thus, beyond the simple English term 'Sabbath,' it carries the depth of a sacred, ordained interruption for rest and consecration.
usageInScripture: The term שַׁבָּתוֹן appears eleven times in Scripture, consistently translated in contexts emphasizing rest or sacred cessation. Most frequently, it is rendered 'of rest' (7 times), highlighting its core meaning. It also appears in phrases like 'shall be a sabbath' and 'shall ye have a sabbath,' indicating its role in divine commands about holy days. This range includes the weekly Sabbath, the Day of Atonement, the sabbatical year, and special feast days, showing its broad application to various divinely appointed times of rest and sanctity.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding שַׁבָּתוֹן enriches our grasp of God's design for rest as a sacred, God-ordained institution that points beyond mere physical repose to spiritual renewal and holiness. It underscores that rest is not optional but commanded, serving as a reminder of God's lordship and provision. This word's use for multiple holy days and sabbatical years illustrates the rhythm God established for His people—a rhythm of work and rest that anticipates the ultimate rest found in Christ. For believers, שַׁבָּתוֹן beckons us to trust in God's sovereignty and to find our true rest in Him, reflecting the eternal Sabbath rest promised in the New Testament.
keyVerseReflection: Exodus 16:23 declares, 'To morrow is the rest of the holy sabbath unto the LORD,' using שַׁבָּתוֹן to emphasize a divinely ordained cessation that is both holy and restorative. The verse instructs preparation in advance, showing that this rest is purposeful and commanded by God. Here, שַׁבָּתוֹן conveys more than a day off; it is a sacred pause to honor the Lord, reinforcing the theme of dependence on God’s provision and the holiness of His appointed times.
